own_solution.law: Bead on a hoop rotating about its vertical diameter: cos(theta0) = g/(Om^2 R), small-oscillation angular frequency Om sin(theta0), T = 2 pi/(Om sin theta0)
assumptions: constant Om with Om^2 R > g

defect_reasons.other: T4B28 ('was set rising with a constant upward acceleration ... before the oscillations were observed') does not state outright that the acceleration persists during the oscillations; the authors' R reading is the natural one but a past-phase reading is possible.

notes: Certified answers verified: base T = 2 pi/(7 sin 60 deg) = 1.03646 s. With g_eff = g + q: q = 1.2 -> cos = 11/19.6, Om_s^2 = 33.566, T = 1.0845 s; q = 2.1 -> T = 1.12963 s; q = 5.6 -> cos = 15.4/19.6, Om_s^2 = 18.75, T = 1.45104 s. All listed q keep g_eff < Om^2 R = 19.6 m/s^2, so the off-axis equilibrium exists. Mass cancellation expression is correct. Minimal pairs T8E51/T4B28 and TD316/T319B share '2.1 m/s²' and differ only in timing/attachment; numeral-free twins T9186 and T9510 as declared. Agrees with pass 1.
